author: Keystone Today
title: Baker and Fritz announce $2.9 million for Susquehanna County transportation projects
text:
Sen. Lisa Baker and Rep. Jonathan Fritz announced on May 13 more than $2.9 million in state funding from the PennDOT Transportation Alternatives Set-Aside program for two projects in Susquehanna County.
The funding will support the construction of concrete curbs and sidewalks along the east side of Route 171 in Lanesboro Borough, starting at the entrance to Susquehanna Community School District’s High School and extending approximately 1,100 feet north to State Route 1009. The new sidewalks and curbs will meet current Americans with Disabilities Act standards to provide a safe walking corridor for students, teachers, and residents.
Additionally, Rail-Trail Council of NEPA, Inc. will receive nearly $1.5 million for a four-mile rail-trail project spanning Ararat and Thompson townships as well as Thompson Borough. Planned improvements include drainage work, resurfacing, trailhead development, access control measures, and new signage along the D&H Rail-Trail.
“This substantial state investment will help us to complete two impactful projects in Susquehanna County,” said Baker. “Funding critical pedestrian improvements in Lanesboro Borough around Susquehanna High School will provide a safer and more accessible walking and biking route for students, teachers and residents. Susquehanna County is also home to some of the best recreational opportunities and outdoor spaces in our commonwealth. The new 4-mile trail that will travel through Ararat and Thompson townships, as well as Thompson Borough will continue to give our families of all ages opportunities to spend more time outdoors while strengthening those communities and improving quality of life.”
Fritz said: “Happy to see the great folks of Lanesboro benefit with this project. Life in a river valley corridor can be challenging, given the topography. These upgrades ensure safety, easy traversing and an increase in property values… This investment in the D&H Rail-Trail continues the buildout of a truly unique and inviting trail system.”
The federal Transportation Alternatives Set-Aside program provides funding for activities such as pedestrian walkways or bicycle facilities that improve non-driver access to public transportation or enhance community mobility.
